problem: Scaling vision-only maps to multi-session, crowdsourced, multi-device capture is hard. Dense or landmark-based maps (point clouds, SfM/ORB landmarks) are costly to store and to re-optimize globally. Single-session VT&R maps cannot fuse sessions. Localization between sessions breaks down under sparse viewpoint overlap, day/night and seasonal appearance change, and cross-device camera differences, and SeqSLAM-style matching assumes contiguous overlapping trajectories.
motivation: Robots deployed long-term need a globally consistent navigation reference that can be continually extended from cheap, ubiquitous cameras (phones, AR glasses, 360 cameras, Street View) rather than LiDAR or GNSS. Recent map-free relocalization and feed-forward 3D geometric foundation models (MASt3R/DUSt3R) can recover local geometry on demand from a few images. This makes it possible to drop stored 3D landmarks and keep only image nodes plus relational edges.
key_idea: Represent the world as a landmark-free, appearance-based topometric map of image nodes linked by three graph layers (covisibility, odometry, traversability). Sessions are merged via DP-based flexible sequence matching plus geometric verification, followed by on-demand MASt3R multi-view pose estimation with residual-calibrated confidence maps. This reduces global estimation to a pose-only PGO, and probabilistic node culling keeps the map bounded.
insight:
Global 3D structure need not be stored if a 3D GFM can re-derive local geometry from 2-3 covisible keyframes on demand. Localization then becomes a pose-graph problem whose loop-closure covariances come from calibrated GFM confidence. Evidence:
- **Topological stage (Tab. results_self_collected):** DP matching with out-of-sequence jumps raises recall where overlap is non-contiguous (CosPlace Ref0 recall 75 vs 58 for SeqSLAM, both with GV), and GV lifts precision sharply (CosPlace DP Ref1 precision 24→78).
- **Merging vs. landmark-based:** on the large R2 region (55 sessions), OpenNavMap reaches 1.51 m ATE with 1 unmerged session, while HLoc-COLMAP merging either diverges (33.87–104.95 m) or drops 21–36 sessions as thresholds tighten.
- **Confidence calibration:** per the metric-localization figures, calibrating confidence (Geman-McClure IRLS) improves precision/AUC over plain DUSt3R/MASt3R global alignment and mitigates the degradation at ≥14 views.
- **Node culling ablation:** IQ-only culling gives the lowest ATE (0.099 m vs 0.105 m without culling). Adding IG and TD trades a little accuracy (0.116 m) for ~20% fewer nodes.
method: Three-layer topometric map: shared image nodes (RGB, global descriptor, timestamp, SE(3) pose, MUSIQ IQA score). Covisibility edges support localization, odometry edges carry relative pose + covariance for PGO, traversability edges carry costs for Dijkstra planning. Each device builds a local submap from any odometry (VIO/SLAM/SfM/GPS), with keyframes every 3.9 m or 60°.

Topological localization: CosPlace ResNet-18 (256-D) descriptors give a cosine difference matrix. A DP shortest-path search allows in-sequence steps (velocity set V) and penalized out-of-sequence jumps (|k|≥Δ, penalty λ) to handle partial or non-contiguous overlap. RANSAC fundamental-matrix geometric verification with MASt3R matches then rejects false pairs.

Metric localization: for each verified pair, 1-2 extra high-covisibility reference nodes are retrieved (N=2-3 images). All MASt3R pairwise pointmaps are computed and a DUSt3R-style global alignment is run over depth, focal, scale and query pose, with reference poses fixed and several hundred gradient steps.

Confidence map calibration: MASt3R confidences are re-weighted each iteration by a Geman-McClure kernel on the per-point residual (IRLS). The mean calibrated weights give a pose covariance Σ=diag[(W̄_ii·W̄_ij)^-2], which is used to keep only high-confidence loop closures (P_CCM).
Pose graph optimization: odometry edges plus inter-submap loop closures are optimized with a robust kernel in GTSAM (Levenberg-Marquardt), merging each query submap into the reference map.

Cross-device handling and lifelong maintenance: perspective rectification of fisheye and equirectangular images, and MUSIQ image-quality prefiltering. Probabilistic node culling uses forward and backward passes combining image quality, 3D-pointmap information gain (fraction of reprojected points outside the reference image) and temporal-difference decay. Covisibility and traversability edges are re-evaluated after each update.

Navigation stack: VPR top-K retrieval + GV gives an anchor node. MASt3R matches + RGB-D back-projection + PnP-RANSAC give the global pose, which is fused with local odometry via PGO. Dijkstra runs over the traversability graph to an image goal, and a local planner (iPlanner in sim, Falco on ANYmal-D) handles obstacle avoidance.

setting.backbone: Off-the-shelf pretrained modules, no fine-tuning: MASt3R (3D GFM, frozen), CosPlace ResNet-18 VPR (frozen), MUSIQ IQA (frozen); local planners iPlanner (sim, learned, frozen) / Falco (real, model-based); GTSAM PGO + Dijkstra planning
setting.training_data: none (training-free); all learned models use public pretrained weights. Maps are built from a self-collected dataset (Meta Project Aria glasses, 18.7 km, 35 sequences over 3.5 months), augmented with iPhone 16 Pro, vehicle camera (FusionPortableV2) and Google Street View panoramas.
setting.observation: Mapping: monocular RGB from heterogeneous devices plus per-session odometry (VIO/SLAM/GPS). Navigation: RGB-D (sim) or ZED2 stereo RGB + depth (real) plus local odometry (ICP in sim; IMU/leg proprioceptive estimator on ANYmal-D).
setting.action_space: Global waypoints = topometric graph nodes (Dijkstra on traversability graph), executed by a local planner (iPlanner / Falco) producing continuous motion
setting.simulator: Matterport3D scenes in a photo-realistic robot simulator (differential-drive robot, 10 Hz RGB-D); Office/Maze/Tunnel occupancy-grid environments for the multi-session planning study; real world (ANYmal-D)
setting.privileged: Navigation uses a pre-built topometric map from prior mapping sessions (pre-exploration). The image goal must correspond to a map node image. Online depth sensor is required. No GT pose at test time (the baseline row uses GT localization).

numbers_note:
Not a standard embodied-navigation benchmark paper: there are no SR/SPL results. The main metric-localization comparisons against HLoc, Reloc3R, DUSt3R and MASt3R on Map-Free, GZ-Campus and Self-Collected (precision and AUC@[1m,10°] vs. number of reference views) appear only in figures. The text says "over 80% precision with only two reference images" on Map-Free. Real-world ANYmal-D navigation is qualitative: 160 m route in "roughly 312s". Inconsistencies in the paper:
- The Exp 2 text says baselines outperform on "the smaller region R2", but the table shows baselines better on R0/R1 and far worse on R2.
- The dataset is said to have 35 sequences in the main text, 37 in the supplement, and the supplement table lists 39.
results: OpenNavMap merges 15.7 km / 110 days of multi-session Aria-glasses data with translational ATE ≤2.87 m across all shuffled orderings and 1.51 m InOrder on R2. The HLoc-COLMAP landmark-based merging baselines reach 3.50–104.95 m ATE on R2 while leaving 21–36 of 55 sessions unmerged. It reports a SoTA 0.62 m average translation error on Map-Free while storing far less: 1.3 MB vs 22.4 MB (HLoc DISK+LG) on scene s00524. DP+GV sequence matching gives the best Avg@1 in most reference sequences vs SeqSLAM and single-frame matching. In simulated image-goal navigation on 3 MP3D scenes, it reaches path lengths close to a GT-localization + Falco baseline (e.g., 223.7 m vs 220.7 m on Env2) with longer times, and it completes real-world ANYmal-D image-goal navigation.
limitations: Online navigation requires a depth source (RGB-D/stereo) for PnP. It only works inside the pre-built map, with no out-of-map/kidnapping recovery. The multi-view GFM optimization is offline, not real-time.

DP sequence matching indexes by traversal order rather than graph topology and becomes an inefficient exhaustive search at scale. 3D GFM accuracy degrades under cross-device, illumination and appearance shifts. At ≥14 views all GFM-based methods decline.

Mapping is centralized, a bottleneck at large scale. Node culling is conservative (~20% reduction) and costs slight accuracy. Evaluation is mostly on the authors' own dataset, with navigation shown on only 12 tasks and no success-rate statistics.
compares_to: single-frame VPR matching (NetVLAD, CosPlace, EigenPlaces, AnyLoc)
